finding.claim: PUT /doc/<doc_id> overwrites a document body without enforcing edit permission. can_edit() is called but its boolean result is discarded, so any authenticated user can modify documents they do not own or edit (IDOR / broken access control).
finding.source: doc_id from the URL path and request.json["body"] from the request body, with the caller identity taken from g.user. Precondition: the caller reaches the route with g.user set (authentication happens outside this file and was not verified).
finding.sink: doc["body"] = request.json["body"] at docs.py:20, which mutates the stored document.

trace.note: Route PUT /doc/<doc_id> is registered with no auth decorator in this file.
doc = DOCS[doc_id] loads the target document by id with no owner or tenant check.
can_edit(g.user, doc) is called but its return value is ignored. No abort(403) or raise follows.
can_edit returns owner == user or user in editors. The result is a boolean that the caller discards.
Attacker-supplied body is written into the document unconditionally.
Returns ok=True, so the unauthorized write succeeds silently.

finding.guards_checked: can_edit at docs.py:7-8 is logically correct (owner or editor) but its result is unused at docs.py:19. The correct pattern, require_edit at docs.py:11-13 which aborts with 403, is used by update_title at docs.py:27 and not by update_doc. No before_request hook or decorator in docs.py enforces authorization. Mass assignment is not possible because only one named field is written. Authentication that sets g.user is outside the reviewed file and was not verified.

verdict.guard_found: None effective. can_edit is defined at docs.py:7-8 and called at docs.py:19, but its boolean return is discarded, so there is no abort. require_edit (docs.py:11-13, aborts with 403) is not called on this route. No before_request hook or decorator in docs.py guards update_doc. Authentication that sets g.user is outside this file and unverified, but it only establishes identity and does not restrict this route.
verdict.reason: update_doc at docs.py:19 calls can_edit(g.user, doc) as a bare statement, so its False result is ignored, and docs.py:20 writes request.json["body"] into the document unconditionally, letting any caller who reaches the route (at minimum an authenticated low-privilege user) modify documents they neither own nor can edit.
